To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the minimum-energy broadcasting problem under practical directional antenna models is NP-Complete and a heuristic algorithm based BIP can be used to solve it efficiently.

the minimum-energy multicast problem under a wide range of practical directional antenna models is NP-Complete, and that antennas with variable orientation and variable beam-width are the best in terms of energy efficiency.
the minimum-energy problem under each directional model is NP-complete and the use of antennas with adjustable orientation gives better broadcast trees than the other antenna models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and analysis of energy-efficient broadcast algorithms in wireless ad hoc and sensor networks.
the practical issues of minimum-energy broadcast in wireless ad hoc and sensor networks and provides a comprehensive study of the problem using various directional antennas.
the practicality of using directional antennas in wireless ad hoc and sensor networks and the design of energy-efficient broadcast protocols under various antenna models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
using smart antennas with variable beamwidth is the most energy-efficient solution to the minimum-energy broadcast.
using directional antennas with adjustable orientation, variable beamwidth, and large number of antenna elements can significantly reduce the broadcast energy cost in all-wireless networks.
, among all the antenna models, using antennas with adjustable orientations and variable beamwidth is the most energy-efficient way to achieve broadcast.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of directional antennas in wireless networks can be very beneficial in terms of reducing the energy consumption for communication.
using smart antennas with a large number of antennas and adjustable orientation can significantly improve the quality of the minimum-energy broadcast trees.
the minimum-energy problem under practical directional antennas is still NP-complete, but it can be solved by a heuristic algorithm that can be easily implemented.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the minimum-energy problem is NP-complete even under the simplest directional antennas with fixed sectors.
the energy efficiency of broadcast communication can be significantly improved by using directional antennas.
using practical antennas that have adjustable orientation and variable antenna beamwidth can achieve significant energy savings in wireless broadcast networks.
